turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Noah Spencer, thanks for the call. Eleno builds custom AI agents for growing Australian businesses, and a first project for a retailer usually lands around $11,200 for a fixed scope build. For a shop like yours that is supplier order drafting, stock alerts and customer enquiry replies handled automatically.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: Thanks Jordan. Lumen Lane Retail is ten people if you count casuals. We sell lighting out of a Prahran showroom and online. I was mostly ringing to hear what this sort of thing costs.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Then you are asking the right question. Most retailers we speak to lose a day a week to reordering and enquiry email. An agent reads the supplier price lists, drafts the purchase order and puts it in front of you to approve. Another answers the lead time questions from the website.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: We are comparing you to a freelancer who set up our stock alerts for a few hundred dollars. He did it in a weekend and it has run since.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: The build also covers what a script never touches. We document the workflow, deploy it into your own systems and transfer the code, so nothing sits on a stranger's laptop. That is the difference between a weekend fix and something you can lean on in December.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: December is busy, but it is two of us and four casuals. Nobody here is drowning in purchase orders.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: A lot of it is invisible. Supplier confirmations, backorder chasing, freight notifications, customer emails about whether a pendant is in stock. Individually two minutes. Across a month it is a part-time role nobody has ever costed.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: We have costed it, roughly. It is maybe four hours a week between the two of us, and a fair bit of that is talking to customers, which we quite like doing.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: The discovery phase would tell us exactly where those hours sit. It is short and paid, we map the workflow, and the build is fixed scope from there. The real number is usually higher than owners expect.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: Paying to be told how long our own admin takes is a hard sell to my co-owner. She does most of the ordering.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: It is not about measuring, it is about designing the agents so they hold up. Skip discovery and you get something brittle that breaks the first time a supplier changes a template. Then you pay twice.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: Our templates barely change. We buy from six suppliers and have done for years.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Six suppliers is a good starting point, because the extraction is simple and we can get the drafting live quickly. We would connect the website enquiries too, so a lead time question gets a drafted reply with the real stock position attached.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: People email us because they want a person. If they get an obviously automated reply about a pendant, that is worse than a slow one.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Ours are drafts, not sends, so a human always approves. The quality is well past what people picture. The bigger risk for a shop your size is staying manual while the chains automate their whole back office.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: We do not really compete with the chains. Our customers come to us because they want someone who knows lighting.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: That expertise is exactly what the agents free up. Every hour on a purchase order is an hour off the showroom floor. I will send the automation overview so you can see what the build includes and what the handover looks like.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: Send it through. I should be straight with you though, eleven thousand is more than we have spent on any system, ever.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Weigh it against the payback. Our average across clients is about six months, so by winter it has paid for itself and the asset stays yours. A subscription is still billing you in year three.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: The subscription part I like. The number is the problem, not the model.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: The number reflects real engineering rather than a template. A scoped build, testing against your actual supplier documents, and the code handed across at the end. A weekend script gives you none of that when it stops.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: If it stops working I will ask him to look at it again. That has been fine so far.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: Until he is unavailable, or moves on, or the business has grown and it no longer fits. That is when most of our retail clients call us, and by then they are rebuilding under pressure.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: Maybe. But we would rather hit that wall than spend the money now on something we might not need.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: The overview sets out a smaller starting scope, just the supplier ordering, which brings the build down. Still a proper engagement with discovery in front of it, but a narrower first step.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: Even narrower, I think we are in a different bracket to your usual client.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: I would not write yourself off. We have built for teams smaller than yours where the owner was the bottleneck. The ones who move early get the compounding benefit.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: I appreciate the pitch, Jordan, but we are going to stay with what we have. It suits how we buy.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Jordan Lee
turns.text: No problem at all. The overview is still worth a read, and it lists the questions to put to any automation provider, including the freelancer, so you can test whether what you have is holding up.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Noah Spencer
turns.text: Fair enough. Thanks for your time.
